title: Getting Started with Minitest
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of getting started with minitest in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply getting started with minitest in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to running a test suite and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Getting Started with Minitest through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding getting started with minitest helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Getting Started with Minitest helps you reason about test structure. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Test structure. Then connect it to Assertions. The remaining syllabus points—Test setup and teardown, Running a test suite—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Getting Started with Minitest
content_blocks.code:
require "minitest/autorun"
class TotalTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_sum
    assert_equal 5, 2 + 3
  end
end
content_blocks.expected_output: 1 runs, 1 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors (format may vary)

items.title: Assuming the happy path is enough
items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule
items.text: Check Ruby version, runtime implementation, and third-party library documentation when behavior is version-sensitive.

items.title: Mixing too many concerns
items.text: Separate input parsing, domain behavior, and output so each piece is easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports getting started with minitest. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for getting started with minitest using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Running a test suite), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain getting started with minitest, identify its place in testing, code quality, and documentation, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
